name: Nebuchadnezzar
bio:
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made Jehoiakim, king of Judah, his vassal; when Jehoiakim later rebelled, the LORD sent raiding bands against Judah as judgment for Manasseh's old sins. After Jehoiakim's death, Nebuchadnezzar's forces besieged Jerusalem under the new king Jehoiachin, who surrendered himself, his mother, and his officials in the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign. Nebuchadnezzar stripped the temple and palace of their treasures, destroyed the gold vessels Solomon had made, and deported Jehoiachin, the royal family, the officials, the craftsmen, and thousands of Jerusalem's leading citizens to Babylon, leaving only the poorest people in the land. He then installed Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, as king, renaming him Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:1-17).

## 📖 Core Story: Destroying Jerusalem

When Zedekiah eventually rebelled, Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem for two years until famine broke the city in his eleventh year. He captured the fleeing Zedekiah near Jericho, executed his sons before his eyes at Riblah, blinded him, and sent him to Babylon in chains. In the fifth month of that same year, Nebuchadnezzar's captain Nebuzaradan burned the temple, the palace, and all of Jerusalem, tore down its walls, carried off the temple's remaining treasures, and deported most of the city's population, leaving only the poorest behind (2 Kings 25:1-21). He then appointed Gedaliah governor over the remnant left in Judah (2 Kings 25:22).
